title: Audit exact union-closed-family certificates on at most four elements
statement: Curator-proposed, pending peer assessment: enumerate every family F subseteq P({1,2,3,4}) with F nonempty, union(F) nonempty, and A union B in F for all A,B in F; for each eligible F record an element x in union(F) such that 2*|{A in F:x in A}| >= |F|. Deliver a completeness argument and an independently implemented verifier. Unused ground elements are allowed; repeated sets are not.
source_locator: Introduction for definitions; section 5 Theorem 17 for the already-known finite-case context.
status_basis: The four-element mathematical property is a special case of the source's reported twelve-element theorem. The certificate/benchmark packaging is a curator proposal; no claim of mathematical novelty or project execution.
plain_summary: Build a small, complete catalog of set families that are closed under union, with a simple witness showing that some element occurs in at least half their sets.
assumptions: Universe U={1,2,3,4}; all smaller-universe families are included by allowing unused elements.
F is a family of distinct subsets, not a multiset.
F is nonempty and union(F) is nonempty, excluding both the empty family and {empty set}.
For every A,B in F, A union B belongs to F; F may or may not contain the empty set.
scope: Curator-proposed benchmark and certificate design, pending peer assessment. Only the at-most-four-element case is covered; its mathematical conclusion is already known.
target: A complete, reproducible certificate catalog and independent checker for the specified finite class, including an exact census keyed by family size and active-universe size.
success_criteria: Specify a bijection between 16-bit masks and all families of subsets of U.
For each eligible union-closed family, supply a witness element meeting the integer inequality in the statement.
Document excluded degenerate families and include cases with and without the empty set.
Provide a completeness argument independent of the result of the main generator.
An independent checker and a human reviewer must agree on definitions, counts, and witnesses; no numbers should be entered as measured before execution.
known_results: The finite conclusion is covered by the survey's Theorem 17 for at most twelve elements. No improvement of that theorem is proposed.
The survey records several equivalent and restricted formulations; this task deliberately fixes the basic set-family formulation.
prerequisites: Power sets and finite set families
significance: The catalog can expose empty-set, quantifier, and encoding mistakes before future work on harder set-system problems. It is research infrastructure with low mathematical novelty.

requirements.data: No empirical or private data. Generated finite families and witnesses become the future artifact.
requirements.compute: Estimated ordinary CPU and small memory. There are exactly 2^16=65,536 input family masks before filtering; this size justifies a conservative laptop-scale planning assumption but is not a timing measurement.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Finite set theory and exact integer arithmetic. Isomorphism reductions, if added, require an explicit proof and must not replace the baseline completeness check.

ai_assessment.rationale: The task has fully bounded enumeration, a local exact witness, and cheap independent verification. Its purpose is to test careful formalization and tooling, not to suggest the general conjecture is easy.

clarity.reason: All degeneracies, allowed elements, and witness conditions are specified.

decomposability.reason: Generator, closure filter, witness finder, census, and checker separate cleanly.

methods.reason: Basic bitset operations suffice; a published survey provides context.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Every object fits in a small exact bit representation.

checkability.reason: Witnesses are integer counts; completeness follows from a fixed finite encoding.

expertise.reason: Basic combinatorics and careful programming are sufficient for this bounded task.

significance.reason: No mathematical novelty; moderate infrastructure value.

verification_difficulty.reason: Most difficulty is proving coverage and avoiding correlated implementation errors.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: No implementation was run. Independent novelty of this packaging is not asserted; existing enumerations may already provide equivalent data.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with exact bitset programming and basic combinatorics.

obstacles: Mistaking the number of sets for the number of ground elements.
Two checkers sharing the same flawed helper or representation assumption.
Using a small-universe result to imply progress on the general conjecture.

steps: Human reviews the domain exclusions and map from masks to families.
Independently reconstruct closure and witness frequency from serialized subsets, avoiding generator helpers.
Compare full enumeration and any symmetry-reduced implementation on the bounded universe.
Check census reconciliation: every input mask is classified once, with exclusion reasons.
Match the verified finite statement to the source's broader known-result context; record it as reproduction.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Low to moderate; independent software and exhaustive-coverage reasoning need careful review.
validation.statement_alignment: Closure is under pairwise union; unused elements are allowed; the witness must lie in union(F); frequency is at least one half, not a strict inequality.

known_attempts: The source survey documents stronger finite cases. No project attempt, certificate census, or AI outcome exists.
unresolved_checks: Review existing public enumeration resources before attributing infrastructure novelty.
Choose certificate schema and independent verifier implementations.
Counts by family size and active-universe size remain unmeasured.
The general union-closed conjecture's present status is outside this card's verification scope.
